title: Fast Pyrolysis of Biomass Residues in a Twin-screw Mixing Reactor
protocol: Activate the whole pyrolysis and condensation system by starting the auxiliary N2 supply and the pyrolysis gas fan.
Flush the pyrolysis test rig with 500 L/hr of nitrogen during standby.
Adjust the nominal volumetric flow in the fan's menu to maintain a reactor pressure 3-8 mbar above ambient pressure.
Fill the bio-oil cycle with an appropriate amount of ethylene glycol as the starting medium for safe pump and homogenizer operation.
Record the weight of the starting material used in the bio-oil cycle.
Fill the aqueous condensate cycle with an appropriate amount of water to allow safe pump operation.
Record the weight of the starting material used in the aqueous condensate cycle.
Heat up the system, including the heat carrier heater and all auxiliary heaters, by entering desired values via their menus (e.g., around 500 °C).
Recommend auxiliary heating for the reactor and connecting pipes to prevent uncontrolled vapor condensation.
Start the cooling cycle for the heat exchangers in both condensation cycles by switching on the cooler.
Open the menus in the process control and click on activate to start the pumps of both condensation cycles.
Adjust the mass flow through the menus to provide enough cooling power.
Recirculate the bio-oil at a rate of around 350 kg/hr and cool it down to 80 °C before spraying it into the quenching vessel.
Recirculate the aqueous condensate at a rate of around 600 kg/hr and supply cooling water at a rate of 300 kg/hr at 8 °C.
Switch on the electrostatic precipitator.
Check the nozzles of the quenching system for blocking after both condensation cycles have run for 10-20 min, and remove any blockage present.
Open the menu of the bucket elevator in the process control and click on activate to start the heat carrier loop.
Open the menu of the heat carrier feeding screw in the process control and click on activate.
Set the heat carrier temperature to a value above the desired reactor temperature for a smoother start-up, accounting for the heat requirements for the pyrolysis reaction.
Supply the heat carrier with a mass flow of 1,000 kg/hr at a temperature of 520 °C during operation, but heat to 545 °C before starting the biomass feed.
After the system has reached set values, fill the biomass storage with desired feedstock.
Open the lock hopper and activate the biomass feeding screw via process control menu.
Slowly increase feed rate to prevent excessive pressure fluctuations.
Record amount of biomass fed for balancing purposes.
Take appropriate samples continuously during operation.
Check reactor temperature (exit temperature of heat carrier) and adjust heating loop accordingly.
Adjust fan nominal volumetric flow to maintain desired reactor pressure.
Check nozzles of quenching system for blocking signs (drop in mass flow or increase in quenching temperature).
Observe pressure drop across cyclones and quenching system to detect scaling early.
Install measures to remove excessive scaling, especially at the first temperature drop point of pyrolysis vapors.
Clean the tube's cross section by using a rod to remove scaling mechanically.
Seal the rod with a gasket to prevent intake of air into the quenching system.
Install a ball valve at the inlet point of the rod to further decrease air leakage if the cleaning is not in operation.
Monitor the condensation temperatures of both condensation cycles.
Adapt the temperature set-points of the process thermostats if necessary.
Remove condensate from cycles as soon as 80% of the maximum allowable filling level has been reached.
Conduct measurements of the gas phase.
Measure the amount of gas.
Measure the composition of the gas including N2, CO, CO2, CH4, O2, and H2.
Turn off the biomass feed.
Regulate the fan to maintain desired reactor pressure.
Allow system (heat carrier loop and condensation cycles) to run for 30-40 min.
Turn off heating of heat carrier loop.
Turn off pumps of both condensation cycles and electrostatic precipitator.
Empty both condensate cycles and record weight of each condensate.
Subtract starting material amount before setting up balances.
Allow containers for char collection to cool down to room temperature in inert atmosphere.
Weigh the amount of char.
Clean bio-oil cycle with fresh ethylene glycol.
Clean aqueous condensate cycle with 1:1 mixture of water and ethanol.
Fill cycles with appropriate amounts (see steps 1.2 and 1.3).
Allow system to run for 30-40 min after cleaning.
Determine the water content of feedstock.
Determine the ash content of feedstock.
Determine the elemental carbon content.
Determine the hydrogen content.
Determine the nitrogen content.
Analyze the water content each experimental day.
Dissolve a sample in dry methanol.
Titrate the dissolved sample with a mixture of base, SO2, and known concentration of I2.
Take a 3,040 g sample of FPBO and dissolve it in methanol to a final volume of about 100 ml.
Stir the solution for 10 min at room temperature.
Filter the solution through a cellulose filter with particle retention of 2.5 µm.
Rinse the residue thoroughly with methanol until a clear filtrate is obtained.
Dry the solid residue at 105 °C overnight and determine its residual weight.
Determine the elemental carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen contents.
Dissolve an FPBO sample in deuterated methanol containing TMSP as a reference material (approximately 0.1 g FPBO in 0.8 g solution).
Centrifuge the dissolved sample to remove solids.
Analyze the sample by 1H nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
Quantify the ethylene glycol content using the peak at 3.55–3.65 ppm for hydroxy groups of ethylene glycol and the reference peak of TMSP around 0 ppm.
